audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Ryze Level 1 and Level 6 and gave Ambessa Levels 4-5 and 2+ items — the exact inverse of what the page's own whys say. whys[3] describes Ryze winning the controlled short trade at 4-5, whys[4] says she controls re-engagement at 6, whys[6] says Ryze wins side-lane skirmishes at two items.
audit.why: Packet levelChart reads Skill/Skill/Ambessa/Ryze/Ambessa/Ambessa/Ryze, which matches the prose. Level 1 is contested rather than Ryze's: Overload's 1000 range beats her 650 Cunning Sweep, but Drakehound's Step closes that for free off any cast.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4 and 6 flipped to Skill/Ryze/Ambessa/Ryze in both layers as matched pairs, ratings moved with them, and the two templated phase whys that now argued the wrong side rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text keyed the whole matchup to a cooldown called "Dash Chain", which does not exist, and spikes[3] contains the typo "sidlane".
audit.why: Drakehound's Step is a passive that triggers off issuing an attack or move command during a cast — there is no chain cooldown to count. The trackable numbers are Repudiation at 18/17/16/15/14 and Public Execution at 130/115/100.
audit.corrected: Spikes rebuilt around Repudiation's 18s rank-1 shield window and the real Q transform (Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam); typo fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Ambessa ability is named correctly anywhere on the page. Everything is attributed to a fabricated "Dash Chain", and the "W-empowered strikes" she supposedly weaves between dashes are actually her Q transform. Repudiation's shield and Public Execution's suppress are never mentioned.
audit.why: Real kit: Drakehound's Step (P) dashes off a cast and empowers the next attack with bonus range, damage and attack speed; Cunning Sweep (Q, 650) transforms into Sundering Slam after it strikes; Repudiation (W, 325, 18s at rank 1) grants a shield, braces, then slams for increased damage if it blocked non-minion damage; Lacerate (E, 325) slows; Public Execution (R, 1250, 130s at rank 1) blinks to the farthest champion in a line, suppresses, then slams and stuns. The shield eats the exact burst Ryze opens with, and the empowered-attack wind-up off Drakehound's Step is the tell to leave.
audit.corrected: Every reference renamed to the real ability, the Q transform stated instead of a phantom W weave, Repudiation named as the shield to bait out, Public Execution given its range/suppress/stun, and Grievous Wounds added to itemization against the healing on her R.

edits.before: Level 1 is a flat loss — you have only Q and must walk into melee range, and Ambessa's passive dash lets her punish any step forward at almost no counterplay cost. Stand at max Q range, farm minions, and bank Manaflow Band stacks; do not throw an auto or W to win a trade you will lose. At level 2 your W root gives you a theoretical deterrent, but Ambessa's dash weaves around the root animation — she can dash through it before it connects if she is already mid-chain. Accept that levels 1–2 are Skill at best and do not blow your only stop on a dash she has already committed to dodge.
edits.after: Level 1 is closer than it feels — Overload throws 1000 units against her 650 Cunning Sweep, so poke on its flat 5s cooldown and never walk the 615 in for Spell Flux, because Drakehound's Step dashes off any cast she makes and empowers the attack that follows. Farm at range and bank Manaflow Band stacks. At level 2 your W root is a deterrent on paper, but Rune Prison only roots a Fluxed target — Flux first or you have bought a slow, and she dashes out of a slow. Accept that levels 1–2 are contested at best and never spend your only stop on a step she has already committed to dodging.

edits.before: Levels 4–5 are where you actually play the matchup: E the minion beside her to apply Flux, then W root the moment Dash Chain is fully spent and she steps in, then empowered Q twice as Phase Rush procs and walk out with the speed boost before her next dash sequence reloads. Never throw W into an active chain — she dashes through it and you are now rootless into a W-empowered striker. Level 6 adds Realm Warp macro threat but gives you no in-lane combat steroid; if she is ahead, use the Warp to relieve pressure by threatening bot rather than trying to solo-kill her top.
edits.after: Levels 4–5 are where you actually play the matchup: E the minion beside her to apply Flux, then W root the moment Repudiation's shield is spent and she steps in, then Q twice as Phase Rush procs and walk out on the speed boost before Lacerate's slow catches you. Never spend W while that shield is bracing — it eats the burst, slams back harder for having blocked it, and you are now rootless in her face. Level 6 adds Realm Warp macro threat but no in-lane combat steroid; if she is ahead, warp pressure onto another lane rather than trying to solo-kill her top.
